patch.value: Validate contributed scalar flag values before extension handler dispatch

A harmless echo fixture declares type bool but --enabled not-a-boolean reaches its handler as a string. Coercion preserves invalid input for later validation, yet current dynamic dispatch validates only allowed/required/disabled option keys. Establish an explicit compatible scalar-validation contract for extension authors.

Define compatibility for invalid number/boolean tokens and optional no-value presence; Apply shared SDK-owned scalar validation before handler invocation where opted in or required by the supported contract; Preserve canonical switch positional behavior and legacy bool grammar; Independently assert malformed value refusals and valid coercion/default/list cases through public CLI/SDK

value.text: Implementation note (2026-10-15): FlagDefinition gains value_validation ("coerce" | "strict"). The default stays the historical passthrough (compatible). strict refuses malformed number/boolean tokens before the extension handler runs with extension_flag_value_invalid (exit 2), naming flag, command path, expected grammar and received token; list entries are checked one by one; a value-less number flag is "received no value". Canonical switch presence and the legacy bool optional-value grammar are preserved: a switch followed by a positional resolves to true and keeps the positional in args. Registration refuses an unknown policy and refuses strict on string/untyped flags because there is nothing to validate; the activation failure surfaces in pm package doctor as extension_activate_failed. Shared SDK helper describeFlagScalarValueFailure is exported through runtime-primitives. Verified via a file-based extension fixture in a sandbox and through the public CLI in integration tests.

patch.value: FlagDefinition.value_validation (coerce default, strict) declared in extension-types, validated at registration (unknown policy and strict on string/untyped flags refused), and enforced before dispatch in the loose option coercer: malformed number/boolean tokens refuse with extension_flag_value_invalid naming flag, command, expected grammar and received token; list entries validated individually; switch presence, --no- negation, the legacy bool optional-value grammar and defaults preserved. Shared helper describeFlagScalarValueFailure exported through runtime-primitives.

Public CLI integration test with a file-based extension: valid coercions, bare legacy bool, switch followed by positional, malformed number/bool/list refusals (exit 2) and activation refusal for strict on a string flag surfaced by pm package doctor; unit tests cover coercer and registration branches. Linked tests pass; exact coverage 100/100/100/100.
Strict scalar validation contract shipped for contributed flags

value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit): strict scalar validation ran after alias folding, so '--limit 5 -l junk' kept the canonical 5 and silently discarded the malformed alias token. Every supplied spelling of a strict non-list scalar is now validated before mergeAliasOptionKeys discards it; a valid alias still yields to the canonical value. Covered in tests/unit/cli/main-loose-options.spec.ts.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit, third pass): two more strict-validation leaks closed. An attached token on a boolean switch (--verbose=maybe) was folded to presence true; the loose tokenizer now marks attached values and a malformed attached token refuses with extension_flag_value_invalid while a following positional keeps presence semantics. An explicitly empty list entry (--ids=, also for repeatable flags) was dropped by list normalization before validation and reached the handler as []; it is now refused before normalization. The coercion loop was split into coerceDefinedLooseOption and helpers to stay under the complexity ceiling, which released one eslint suppression (ceiling 106 to 105).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review follow-up (PR #1479, CodeRabbit, fourth pass): on a strict CSV list, an empty segment inside one token (--ids=1,,2) was dropped by flattenFlagListValue before validation. refuseEmptyStrictListEntries now splits CSV occurrences on commas before the empty-entry check, while repeatable flags keep commas inside one occurrence so the whole token is reported as the malformed value. Covered in tests/unit/cli/main-loose-options.spec.ts.
